title: Mobile backend modernization
subtitle: Kotlin + Spring Boot rewrite using hexagonal architecture
overview: I rewrote the backend for a long-lived KMP mobile app, moving from Java + MyBatis to Kotlin + Spring Boot. The goal was practical: make the code easier to change, safer to run, and faster to reason about. The rewrite reduced boilerplate and improved day-to-day developer ergonomics.
challenge: The old backend carried a decade of patches: business logic mixed in MyBatis mappers, different database dialects, and fragile upgrade paths. Small changes could ripple across systems. Shipping reliable fixes took too long.
solution: I rewrote the service in Kotlin with Spring Boot and Kotlin Exposed. I focused on small, testable modules and a hexagonal structure so the core logic lives alone and adapters do the dirty work. That made tests simpler, database changes safer, and future refactors less scary.

keyAchievements.title: Cleaner language
keyAchievements.description: Moved the codebase to Kotlin. Less boilerplate, clearer null handling, and more expressive APIs made daily work noticeably faster.

keyAchievements.title: Safer database access
keyAchievements.description: Replaced MyBatis with Kotlin Exposed to get compile-time type checks for queries and fewer runtime surprises.

keyAchievements.title: Hexagonal architecture
keyAchievements.description: Separated business rules from I/O (API, DB). That paid off immediately: I could run unit tests without spinning up databases.

keyAchievements.title: Multi-database compatibility
keyAchievements.description: Kept compatibility with MySQL, Oracle and SQL Server while moving the code to a single, consistent data-access layer.

keyAchievements.title: Practical quality gains
keyAchievements.description: Introduced consistent error handling, better logging, and test containers for integration tests — real things that make debugging less painful.

learnings: Small, opinionated conventions beat vague patterns when multiple DBs are involved.
Hexagonal boundaries make refactors low-risk. I wish I'd done this sooner.
Type-safe queries save time during debugging — the IDE becomes your friend.
Backward compatibility matters: we kept the old DBs while moving forward.
